summary: PII redaction failures during canary rollout of quantized-llama-3 at OmegaRetail (major incident)
description:
Issue summary: During a canary rollout of quantized-llama-3-13b (q4_0) to OmegaRetail's dedicated pool, several customer requests returned unredacted PII where the expected anonymization/redaction rules should have been applied. Impact: potential exposure of email addresses and order IDs in streaming completions for ~0.4% of canary requests. Environment: OmegaRetail dedicated cluster (prod, us-east-1), traffic routed via dedicated canary target group.

Reported by customer: 2026-03-10 13:12 UTC. Customer noticed raw email addresses appearing in generated responses in logs and alerted Support via phone and #support-escalations.

Template fields included below: Issue summary, Impact, Environment, Steps to reproduce, Observed logs. See "steps_to_reproduce" and "logs" fields for structured reproducer information.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send canary request to omega-retail workspace using model=quantized-llama-3-13b-q4_0 with redaction pipeline enabled.
2) Use prompt with placeholder for customer contact: 'Contact: user@example.com' and ask model to summarize order.
3) Observe output: redaction step should replace email with <REDACTED> but returns original with minor token-boundary changes.
4) Re-run with stable model (llama-3-13b-base) and observe correct redaction behavior.
timeline: 2026-03-10 13:12 UTC - OmegaRetail support call; 13:20 UTC - Support triage ticket created; 13:35 UTC - SRE throttled canary traffic and enabled 100% routing to stable pool; 13:50 UTC - Rollback of quantized model canary completed; 14:10 UTC - Customer confirm no further unredacted items in live requests; 2026-03-11 - Internal investigation continues; 2026-03-13 - Hotfix deployed and verified; ticket moved to Resolved.
impact: Customer-facing safety regression: a subset of generated completions bypassed post-processing redaction rules, exposing PII (emails, order references). Affected ~0.4% of canary requests for ~2 hours. Regulatory concern raised by OmegaRetail compliance team; requested immediate remediation and follow-up artifacts for audit.
logs:
[2026-03-10T13:18:42Z] request_id=abc123 model=quantized-llama-3-13b-q4_0 workspace=omega-retail prompt_snippet='Customer email: user@example.com' result_snippet='Contact user@example.com regarding order #A-323' postproc_status=redaction_mismatch kernel=quant-kernel-v3
[2026-03-10T13:19:10Z] request_id=abc456 model=llama-3-13b-base postproc_status=redaction_success result_snippet='Contact <REDACTED> regarding order <REDACTED>'
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: quantized runtime changed tokenization boundaries causing the post-processing redaction regex (designed against original tokenizer output) to miss matches.
Evidence: token-level diffs show that '@' and '.' characters were split across tokens in q4_0 outputs, producing variants not matched by our canonical redaction patterns.
Additional finding: canary traffic exercised a new kernel (quant-kernel-v3) that applies a faster subword packing optimization; this optimization sometimes emits fused tokens at chunk boundaries. Post-processing service assumed whitespace-delimited token boundaries when applying redaction regex.
We reproduced locally by running quantized runtime with sample prompt and comparing token stream to non-quantized runtime. Confirmed mismatch.
Related: a small misconfiguration in the canary routing rules allowed 5% of canary traffic to hit an older postproc configuration lacking the normalization-pass (operator omitted in the canary container image).
mitigation:
Immediate actions: 1) SRE paused canary and routed all traffic to stable (llama-3-13b-base) at 13:35 UTC. 2) Applied emergency policy to reject any model rollout that doesn't pass PII-safety gate in the canary pipeline. 3) Issued temporary account-level hold for OmegaRetail canary traffic until validation completed. 4) Provided customer with credits for impacted window and produced log export for compliance.
Customer communications: initial notification within 30 minutes; formal incident summary and credits email within 24 hours.
resolution:
Rolled back quantized model canary and disabled quant-kernel-v3 on dedicated pool. Deployed hotfix v1.2.7-hotfix: adds tokenization normalization step in post-processing that maps fused/packed tokens back to canonical representation prior to regex redaction; added unit and integration tests (PII test corpus) to CI. Updated canary container images to include normalization-pass and a canary-only PII-safety test that runs against a seeded corpus.
Post-deploy verification: ran seeded tests and live canary for 24 hours in a staging mirror; zero redaction misses observed. Customer validated exported logs and received compliance artifact.
Longer-term: updated rollout checklist and added automated telemetry alerts for 'postproc_redaction_mismatch' metric to high-priority SRE dashboard.
postincident_action_items: Add tokenization-normalization step to post-processing library and runbook
Improve canary image diff check to prevent omitting postproc operator
Add PII-safety gate to automated canary smoke tests (must pass before >0% production traffic)
Create metric alert for postproc_redaction_mismatch with P0 escalation policy
Share incident and runbook updates with enterprise customers via customer advisory

notes_for_postmortem: Root cause is twofold: (1) quantized kernel token packing produced token sequences that bypassed existing regex-based redaction; (2) canary pipeline image drift omitted normalization operator. Corrective measures include code fix, CI test coverage, and canary validation improvements. Postmortem to be published to Confluence and linked from this ticket.
